issues.legal_issue: An authorised officer may confiscate tools and implements used to commit a forest offence when state-owned forest produce connected with the offence is produced before the officer.
material_facts: Timber alleged to have been illicitly felled and removed from a forest was seized from a sawmill along with a band saw and other implements.
The authorised officer found that the timber was state property, that a forest offence had been committed in respect of it, and that the band saw and implements had been used in the offence.

The authorised officer ordered confiscation of the timber and the tools and implements. The finding that the tools and implements were used in the offence was not disturbed by the High Court, and the timber confiscation was conceded there.
The High Court set aside the confiscation of the tools and implements, relying on an earlier decision concerning a sawmill and machinery confiscated independently of state-owned forest produce.
issues.conclusion: The High Court erred in setting aside the confiscation of the band saw and implements. The appeal was allowed and the High Court judgment was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 59A(3) of the Indian Forest Act, 1927, as amended in West Bengal, when state-owned timber or other forest produce is produced before an authorised officer and the officer is satisfied that a forest offence has been committed in respect of it, the officer may confiscate that produce together with tools and other items used in committing the offence. Confiscation is a separate proceeding and does not depend on whether a prosecution is instituted. The Court applied Divisional Forest Officer v. G. V. Sudhakar Rao, AIR 1986 SC 328, and distinguished Subhash Rai v. State of West Bengal because that case concerned machinery sought to be confiscated independently of state-owned forest produce and without the relevant finding of a forest offence.

rule.if: forest_confiscation_appeal and state_owned_forest_produce_produced and officer_found_offence_concerning_produce and tools_used_in_offence

predicates.forest_confiscation_appeal: A party appealed a judgment that had set aside an authorised officer’s order confiscating property in a forest-offence matter.
predicates.state_owned_forest_produce_produced: State-owned timber or other forest produce connected with the alleged offence was produced before the authorised officer.
predicates.officer_found_offence_concerning_produce: The authorised officer was satisfied that a forest offence had been committed in respect of the state-owned forest produce.
predicates.tools_used_in_offence: The authorised officer found that the tools or implements at issue had been used to commit the forest offence.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a judgment setting aside confiscation, state-owned forest produce was produced, the authorised officer found an offence concerning it, and the tools were used in that offence, confiscation of those tools is authorized.
